lessons.title: The five senses and the skeleton

blocks.title: The five senses
blocks.md: We have five senses: **sight** (eyes), **hearing** (ears), **smell** (nose), **taste** (tongue) and **touch** (skin). They tell us about the world around us and warn us of danger: we smell smoke, hear a horn and feel a hot pot.

blocks.caption: The five senses.
blocks.alt: A table with five rows: sight and eyes, hearing and ears, smell and nose, taste and tongue, touch and skin, with what each does.

blocks.title: The skeleton
blocks.md: The **skeleton** is the frame of **bones** inside the body. It **supports** the body, **protects** soft parts (the skull protects the brain; the ribs protect the heart and lungs) and, with **muscles**, helps us **move**. Bones meet at **joints** such as the knee and elbow. An adult has about 206 bones.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that muscles are the same as bones: muscles pull on bones to make them move.
- Looking at the sun or using sharp objects near the eyes.
- Using sticks or pins in the ears.
- Forgetting that skin is also a sense organ.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Which sense do you use to know that tea is too hot?
steps: The skin of the lips and tongue feel the heat.
It is the sense of touch.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Which part of the skeleton protects the brain?
steps: The brain is inside the head.

objectives: Name the food groups and give local examples.

reviewNotes: Health and hygiene advice is conservative and general; it must be reviewed by a health worker or a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Food groups
blocks.md: We eat to get **energy**, to **grow** and to stay **healthy**. **Energy foods**: cassava, yam, rice, maize, plantain. **Body-building foods** (proteins): beans, groundnuts, fish, eggs, meat. **Protective foods** (vitamins and minerals): fruits and vegetables such as eru, okra, orange and pawpaw. We also need a little **fat or oil** and plenty of **safe water**.

blocks.caption: Food groups with examples from Cameroon.
blocks.alt: A table of four food groups, their jobs and local examples: energy foods, body-building foods, protective foods, fats and oils.

blocks.title: Balanced diet and digestion
blocks.md: A **balanced diet** has a little of each food group in the right amounts. **Digestion** breaks food into tiny parts that the blood can carry. Food goes from the **mouth** (teeth chew it) to the **food pipe**, **stomach**, **small intestine** (food is absorbed) and **large intestine**; waste leaves the body.

blocks.caption: The path of food through the body.
blocks.alt: Five boxes joined by arrows from top to bottom: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Eating only one kind of food, such as only starch.
- Thinking that sweets and fizzy drinks are healthy because they give energy: too much sugar harms teeth.
- Swallowing food without chewing.
- Forgetting to wash fruit and vegetables.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Put the foods in groups: rice, beans, orange, groundnut oil.
steps: Rice gives energy; beans build the body; orange protects; groundnut oil is a fat/oil.
Match each food to its job.
blocks.answer: rice: energy; beans: body-building; orange: protective; groundnut oil: fats and oils.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: Food is first chewed by the teeth and mixed with saliva.

blocks.title: Personal hygiene
blocks.md: Hygiene means keeping clean to stay healthy. **Wash your hands with soap and water** before eating and after using the toilet. **Bathe** often, **brush your teeth** twice a day, keep **nails short** and wear clean clothes. Always **drink safe water** (boiled, filtered or treated) and **wash fruit and vegetables**.

items.text: Wash hands with soap and water
Drink safe water, eat clean food
Keep the house and yard clean

blocks.caption: Four healthy habits.
blocks.alt: Four boxes with healthy habits: wash hands with soap and water; drink safe water and eat clean food; sleep under a mosquito net; keep the house and yard clean.

blocks.title: Preventing malaria
blocks.md: Malaria is spread by the **bite of a mosquito**. We can prevent it by **sleeping under a mosquito net**, **clearing stagnant water** and bushes near the house (where mosquitoes lay eggs) and covering water containers. If someone has fever, tell an adult and go to the **health centre**. Do not take medicine without a health worker's advice.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that malaria comes from the sun, cold or eating mangoes: it comes from mosquito bites.
- Washing hands only with water and no soap.
- Drinking water from the stream or a pond without making it safe.
- Treating fever by yourself instead of going to the health centre.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Why must we wash our hands before eating?
steps: Our hands pick up germs from things we touch.
Washing with soap removes germs, so we do not swallow them with our food.
blocks.answer: To remove germs and avoid tummy infections.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A puddle has been in the yard for a week. Why is it a danger?
steps: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water.
More mosquitoes mean more risk of malaria: empty or drain the puddle.
blocks.answer: Mosquitoes breed in it, and they spread malaria.
